knowledgeAnswers.rationale: An out-of-date tag means the scaffold is not cleared for use. A competent individual must check it again.
A missing guardrail on an open edge is a fall control gap. The other options describe a scaffold in good order.
Locked castors stop the tower moving under load. The need does not depend on a tower's height.
The tags and handover section says a scaffold should carry a tag showing whether it can be used safely, who checked it and when.

practicalCriteria: Walks a supplied scaffold or tower and reports each planted defect by name
Checks a mobile tower's castors, brakes, outriggers, boarding and tag before climbing
Refuses use of a tower with an out-of-date or missing tag, and records the stop
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed check record for a supplied tower
stopWorkCriteria: A scaffold with a missing guardrail or an out-of-date tag is not used
A mobile tower with an unlocked castor or an unlevel base is not climbed
